ECONOMICS · LAUREATE 01

CONSUMPTION · EXPECTATIONS · MICROFOUNDATIONS

Robert E.Hall.

An American economist whose work connected forward-looking household choices to the macroeconomic models used to understand business cycles and stabilisation.

Start the study lensEconomics overview
FIELDMacroeconomics · consumption · labour
AFFILIATION AT AWARDStanford University
CORE QUESTIONHow do expectations shape present household choices?

WHY HE MATTERS

Build macro behaviour from household decisions

Hall showed how forward-looking consumers adjust current spending in response to new information about future income. This gave macroeconomic analysis a disciplined microeconomic foundation and helped connect individual expectations to aggregate demand and economic fluctuations.

I
INPUT

Income news and expectations

Households update beliefs about resources available now and in the future.

P
PROCESS

Intertemporal choice

Consumers balance spending and saving across time under uncertainty.

O
OUTPUT

Aggregate consumption dynamics

Individual choices become a testable building block for macroeconomic stabilisation models.

THREE-PASS REVIEW

Read Hall’s contribution from three angles

ACTIVE LENS

The household

A forward-looking household bases consumption not only on today’s income but also on what it learns about future resources. New information—not a mechanical calendar—drives revisions.

VERIFIED READING

Follow the evidence
